title: Choose segmented transfer granularity before flattening per-element indices

source.title: Sealed structured-mask A/B refinement of vLLM PR #55469 transfer
source.claim_scope: One sealed SM89 task showed that elementwise segmented indices can lose to contiguous spans; it is a routing refinement, not a target speedup guarantee.

implementation_recipe: Classify each segment as element synthesis, contiguous source-to-destination span, general permutation or full-coverage identity before choosing vectorization.
Estimate auxiliary index bytes and construction passes per payload byte; do not build repeated int64 per-element indices when one slice or run descriptor moves a wide contiguous payload.
Implement the cheapest semantic tier first: full-coverage identity/no-fill, whole-array permutation, coalesced span copies, then general flattened scatter.
Retain a measured sparse/small fallback and dispatch only across a frozen per-shape frontier.
validation_recipe: Test empty, sparse, permuted, absent-segment and full-coverage cases with irregular segment lengths.
Report auxiliary index allocation and bytes in addition to payload bytes.
Benchmark sparse and full-coverage cells independently; reject a weighted winner that breaches the protected per-shape guard.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Full coverage can remove initialization and index staging, exposing only payload copy and H2D cost.
Span coalescing reduces Python row dispatch without introducing O(total elements) int64 index construction.
General scatter remains appropriate only when irregularity prevents cheaper identity, permutation or span forms.
failure_modes: A per-element repeat/cumsum construction allocates more auxiliary bytes than the payload and loses on sparse or wide rows.
A full-coverage fast path assumes compact request order already equals destination order.
Coalescing spans across an absent request consumes the wrong compact source rows.
One aggregate speedup hides a severe small-batch or sparse-selection regression.
scope_limits: The sealed experiment is one SM89 task and does not establish a universal crossover.
Element-synthesis workloads such as local offset generation may still favor full flattened segmented-array construction.

algorithmic_decomposition.baseline_dependency: Each logical segment maps either generated elements or one contiguous source row range to a destination range.
algorithmic_decomposition.partition_axis: maximal runs sharing source and destination contiguity plus a separate full-coverage identity cell
algorithmic_decomposition.combine_rule: Coalesce adjacent affine spans; use a whole-array permutation when one destination vector suffices, and expand per-element indices only for genuinely irregular scatter or synthesis.
algorithmic_decomposition.finalization: Stage the chosen pinned payload and optional compact int32 indices through the unchanged H2D boundary.
algorithmic_decomposition.work_complexity: O(number_of_segments + payload_items), while avoiding extra O(payload_items) int64 arrays on contiguous-span cells.
algorithmic_decomposition.span_complexity: Identity is one bulk copy, a coalesced plan is one operation per maximal run, and only the irregular fallback spans the flattened index space.
algorithmic_decomposition.communication_cost: Mandatory payload H2D is unchanged; optional output-index traffic is removed for full coverage.
invariants: absent segments consume source but do not write
anti_patterns: one int64 index vector per payload dimension
apply identity fast path from set equality without order proof

candidate_archetypes.name: proved full-coverage no-fill path
candidate_archetypes.template: When compact rows already cover destination rows in exact order, skip -1 fill and optional indices and copy the payload as one array.

candidate_archetypes.name: maximal contiguous run copies
candidate_archetypes.template: Copy one slice per maximal affine source/destination run instead of expanding per-element scatter indices.

candidate_archetypes.name: irregular flattened scatter fallback
candidate_archetypes.template: Build one bounded destination/source mapping only for irregular cells where its measured gain exceeds auxiliary construction cost.
